text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- The government will provide some $5 million towards HIV-AIDS prevention this year, the National AIDS Committee has announced.
-- Deputy Prime Minister Nguyen Khanh has received a delegation from China's Academy of Social Sciences.

-- Economic relations between Vietnam and Hongkong will accelerate following the British colony's return to China later this year, a senior manager at the Hongkong Trade Development Council said in a meeting last week in Ho Chi Minh City.

-- Petrovietnam will build Vietnam's first oil refinery at Dung Quat in Quang Ngai Province, despite the financial difficulties and even if it has to do so without foreign participation, according to the company's director general.
-- Vietnam airlines will use Boeing 767-300 and Airbus A320 planes for flights between Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City from March 30 when a summer flight schedule begins.
-- Vietnam and China have agreed to begin regular cross-border train services between Hanoi and Kunming from April 18.

-- Vietnam has asked China to immediately withdraw the Kan Tan 111 oil rig and supporting vessels from an area inside Vietnam's exclusive economic zone and continental shelf, a Vietnamese lawyer said in an interview with Vietnam News Agency.
-- Ho Chi Minh City's Court of Appeal will begin examining sentencing today in a corruption case surrounding the Tamexco trading firm.
-- An Austrian parliamentary delegation will visit Vietnam in the near future.
